text_blocks.snippet: Scammers in Central Illinois are actively using artificial intelligence (AI) voice cloning, number spoofing, and fake government or police impersonation to target residents and steal personal and financial information.
snippet_highlighted_words: artificial intelligence (AI) voice cloning, number spoofing, and fake government or police impersonation

text_blocks.snippet: Common Scam Types in Central Illinois

list.snippet: AI Voice & Impersonation Scams: Scammers use AI to clone human voices, pretending to be family members in distress or law enforcement officers (such as fake detectives claiming you have an active arrest warrant).

Official Phone & Number Spoofing: Scammers spoof phone numbers belonging to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois, local sheriff's offices, or city departments to demand immediate payments or cash bonds.
Fake Traffic & Tollway Text Messages: Fraudulent texts claim you owe money for a traffic or tollway violation and push you to click a link or hand over credit card data.
City & Zoning Board Invoices: Scammers target residents who recently appeared before local boards (like in Pekin, IL) with fake invoices or notices on forged city letterhead.
Social Media & Online Shopping Frauds: Fake profiles pretend to be real businesses offering steep discounts or trending merchandise.
Urgency & Secrecy: Demands that you act immediately, pay right away, or stay on the phone without talking to family.
Unusual Payment Methods: Requests to pay via gift cards, wire transfers, cryptocurrency, or peer-to-peer apps (which are nearly impossible to reverse).
Unsolicited Contact: Government agencies, the IRS, and police departments do not call, text, or email out of the blue to demand money or sensitive data.
Establish a Safe Word: Create a secret code word with your family members to verify identities during unexpected phone calls asking for help or money.
Hang Up and Verify: Do not trust caller ID. Hang up and call the official phone number of the agency, court, or business directly.
Practice the Pause: Slow down and talk to a trusted friend or family member before sending any money or sharing personal details.

text_blocks.snippet: What to Do If You Have Been Scammed

list.snippet: Stop all communication immediately with the suspected scammer.
Do not send any additional funds or read off gift card or bank numbers.
Contact your bank or credit union right away to freeze accounts or dispute charges if financial info was shared.
Report the fraud to the Illinois Attorney General's Office or call their Consumer Fraud Hotlines:
Springfield: 1-800-243-0618
Chicago:
Carbondale: 1-800-243-0607
Spanish-language: 1-866-310-8398
File a report with your local police department or county sheriff's office.

text_blocks.snippet: If you or someone you know received a specific suspicious call, text, or letter, tell me what type of message it was (e.g., a fake arrest threat, a text about a package, or an invoice) so I can give you the exact steps to handle it.
